findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The expo preparation cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 58F in the bottom and potato salad was probed to be at 54F in the top of the cooler. The PIC stated that they were using an ice bath to cold hold TCS food items in the cooler. CORRECTED- The PIC voluntarily discarded all TCS food items in the cooler and placed new food items on ice baths. It was discussed to make sure that all staff are educated to use an ice bath until the preparation cooler is repaired. Ensure that TCS food items are cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The small preparation cooler is observed to be holding at an ambient temperature of 58F. Potato salad in the top of the preparation cooler was probed to be at 54F. findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were raw, shelled eggs above containers of sauces in the double-door cooler in the dish area. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the eggs to the bottom shelf of the cooler and proper storage order was discussed. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The cooler drawers on the cook-line were observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. Salmon in the bottom cooler drawer was probed at 50F and beef patties in the top cooler drawer were probed at 49F. According to the PIC, the temperature of the cooler drawers were last checked at 12pm and were observed to be at 39F. The TCS food items in this cooler were placed under Time as Control. It was discussed to use or discard the items by 4pm. The PIC stated that they will cook all of the food items before 4pm. 

The front preparation cooler in the kitchen was observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F. A salad dressing in the top of the preparation cooler was probed at 54F and bread was probed in the bottom of the preparation cooler at 58F. According to the PIC, the temperature of the cooler was last checked at 12pm and was at 37F. The TCS food items in the cooler were placed under Time as Control. It was discussed to use or discard the items in this cooler by 4pm. 

Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The cooler drawers were observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F and the front preparation cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F. TCS food items in the cooler drawers were probed to be at 50F and 49F and TCS food items in the front preparation cooler were probed to be at 54F and 58F. These food items were placed under Time as Control (see violation #22). A follow up is scheduled on 7/13/2026 to ensure that these coolers have been repaired and are properly cold holding at 41F and below. The top of the front preparation cooler was observed to be being left open when not in use. The kitchen is observed to be extremely hot and it is highly recommended to leave cooler doors closed when they are not actively in use. It is also recommended to check the internal temperatures of coolers at least every two hours to make sure that TCS foods are being properly cold held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There is not a probe thermometer available to use in the facility. This was discussed with the PIC, who will be ordering another one. A follow up is scheduled for 7/13/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer to accurately measure the internal temperature of foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The Certified Food Protection Manager left for a meeting during the inspection. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to be sweeping the floor and then use their bare hands to season cooked fries. CORRECTED- The fries were discarded and the employee was educated to never use their bare hands to contact ready-to-eat foods (see violation #9). The employee was also educated that handwashing should always be done when switching tasks, especially when going from sweeping to food preparation or cooking. Ensure that all employees are educated on washing hands when switching tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to be sweeping, then use their bare hands to season cooked fries. CORRECTED- The fries were discarded. The employee was educated that ready-to-eat food items should never be touched with bare hands and that handwashing is needed when going from sweeping to any type of food preparation or cooking. Ensure that all staff are educated on never using their bare hands to touch ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The kitchen dish machine was observed to initially test at 0ppm of Chlorine. The dish machine had been in the process of being used to clean dishes when it was tested. The dish machine had to be primed and it tested at 50ppm of Chlorine. Discussed with the PIC that the dish machine should be being tested daily to ensure that dishes are being properly sanitized. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: There was reduced oxygen packaged salmon observed to be in the bottom of the cooler that was still in its packaging. Reduced oxygen packaged salmon should be removed from its reduced oxygen environment before being thawed to reduce the risk of botulism. CORRECTED- The staff were educated on this and the salmon in the cooler drawer all had a slit placed in it. Ensure that staff are educated on proper thawing procedures for reduced oxygen packaged fish.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the CFPM to not have an allergen certification. Ensure all CFPMs have valid allergen certifications. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: REPEAT- The dish machine in the bar area was observed to only dispense 0-10ppm of chlorine sanitizer. The proper concentration is 50-200ppm. A follow up will be conducted on 10-30-2024 to ensure that the dish machine is dispensing at the proper concentration. Until the dish machine is repaired, use the triple sink to properly sanitize dishes.

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The soda nozzles were observed to have soiled residue buildup. CORRECTED- All of the soda nozzles were removed and cleaned. Ensure that soda nozzles are removed and cleaned regularly to prevent future buildup of soils.

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: The bread freezer was observed to have ice buildup on the floors and fans. Make sure that ice is removed to create smooth and easily cleanable surfaces. Ensure that the unit is serviced to prevent future ice build up.

(A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The vents above the cook line were observed to be heavily soiled with dust buildup. Ensure that ceiling vents are cleaned and maintained clean in all areas where food is prepped.

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The following physical facilities were observed to be in need of being cleaned: 

1. Shelves in dry storage were observed to be dusty. Ensure shelves are regularly cleaned to prevent accumulation of dust and debris.

2. Wall around dish machine was observed to have a buildup of soil residues. Ensure that this wall is cleaned and maintained cleaned. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained clean.


(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Upon arriving at the facility to follow-up on previous violations, inspector attempted to use the hand sink before checking the sanitizer concentration of the dish machine.  There was a basket in the sink, it was being used as a dump sink.  Inspector discussed with PIC, COS.  Ensure the hand sink is not used for anything but hand washing.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The chlorine sanitizer concentration for the bar dishwasher was 0 ppm for two runs during inspection.  Discussed with PIC, who primed the lines, yet the concentration was still 0 ppm.  The company had been out to service the machine after the last inspection and stated it was working.  The company who services the machine was contacted during the inspection and will contact inspector when it is running properly.  Ensure employees are monitoring the concentration with test strips to ensure the correct concentration is being dispensed.  Also train all employees on how to operate the dish machine so it sanitizes the dishes.  Inspector will follow-up on the dish machine in 3 days.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFPM was present during today’s inspection.  Ensure a CFPM is present and on-site during all hours of operation.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
It was observed during the inspection that the hot holding food items on the steam table were 90F.  After discussing with an employee, it was noticed that the breaker was tripped and that they had been having problems with all day.  All items were removed and moved to the oven.  PIC contacted an electrician during the inspection.  Ensure the electrical is properly repaired, do not use the steam table until it is working properly.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The temperature of the double door cooler holding all of the prepped foods and sauces was observed to have an internal temperature of 50F.  Inspector came back at the end of the inspection to recheck the temperature after the door had remained shut, but it had not changed.  Multiple internal temperatures were taken, all showing 50-55F.  All items were discarded, except for items that were prepped on this day.  The PIC stated a work order had already been put in for multiple pieces of equipment, including this cooler.  Do not use this cooler until it is working properly. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Multiple flies were observed in the mop room.  Ensure pest control is contacted to eradicate the flies and prevent food contamination.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Baffles were observed to contain an accumulation of grease and dust debris. Not cleaning the baffles in between service dates can cause accumulation of debris and possible food contamination.  Ensure baffles are cleaned routinely in between service dates.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The fan used on the cook line was observed to contain an accumulation of dust and food debris.  Ensure the fan is cleaned frequently to prevent contamination of food on the cook line.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.
